newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian parliament elects Kostov as premier.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian parliament elects Kostov as premier.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament appointed on Wednesday the leader of the Union of Democratic Forces Ivan Kostov as prime minister.
Of 233 deputies present, 179 deputies voted for, 54 were against and none abstained.
In two separate votes parliament approved Kostov's cabinet lineup and restructuring programme.
Of 234 deputies present, 179 voted for the new cabinet, 55 voted against and none abstained.

Kostov is keeping on five ministers from the interim cabinet, including deputy premier and industry minister Alexander Bozhkov and interior minister Bogomil Bonev who will continue his campaign against crime and high-level corruption.
Defense minister Georgi Ananiev, Transport Minister Wilhelm Kraus and Social Policy minister Ivan Neikov retain their jobs.
Muravei Radev, 50, head of the previous parliament's budget and finance committee, is finance minister, and UDF deputy leader Nadezhda Mihailova as foreign minister.
The former ruling Socialists, who now hold 58 seats and were widely blamed by Bulgarians for the country's economic collapse, voted against Kostov's cabinet.

"This is a single-party cabinet and does not correspond to the widely advertised idea for national consensus and harmony between politicians and professionals," Socialist deputy Roumen Ovcharov told Reuters.

Kostov's programme focuses on speeding up economic reform, improving social welfare, fighting organised crime, opening files concerning public figures, returning land to pre-communist owners and bringing Bulgaria into the European Union and NATO.
